title: Question 2
stem: An ideal gas has pressure $p$, volume $V$ and absolute temperature $T$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the basic assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases.

markscheme_points.text: Any two from: molecules in continuous random motion; volume of molecules negligible compared to volume of gas; elastic collisions; no intermolecular forces except during collision; collision time negligible compared to time between collisions

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in kinetic theory assumptions that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the amount of gas, in mol, in a container of volume $0.045\text{ m}^3$ at pressure $1.2 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$ and temperature $290\text{ K}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in kinetic theory assumptions connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Kinetic theory assumptions. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$pV = nRT \implies n = pV / (RT) = (1.2 \times 10^5 \times 0.045) / (8.31 \times 290)$; $n = 2.24\text{ mol}$ (accept $2.2\text{ mol}$)
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) speed of the gas molecules of molar mass $0.028\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in kinetic theory assumptions connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: $\frac{1}{2} M c_{\text{rms}}^2 = \frac{3}{2}RT \implies c_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT / M} = \sqrt{3 \times 8.31 \times 290 / 0.028}$; $c_{\text{rms}} = 508\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (accept $510\text{ m s}^{-1}$)

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the total internal energy of the gas in the container.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in kinetic theory assumptions connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Kinetic theory assumptions. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$U = \frac{3}{2}nRT$ or $U = \frac{3}{2}pV$; $U = 1.5 \times 1.2 \times 10^5 \times 0.045$; $U = 8100\text{ J}$ (or $8.1\text{ kJ}$)
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The gas is heated at constant pressure. Explain why the thermal energy supplied is greater than the increase in internal energy.

markscheme_points.text: gas expands against atmospheric pressure as temperature rises
work is done by the gas on the surroundings ($W = p\Delta V$)
first law $\Delta Q = \Delta U + W$ so thermal energy supplied $\Delta Q$ must exceed increase in internal energy $\Delta U$
